original_title: As Resident Evil Requiem Passes $500m Revenue, Analysis Shows 8.6% Sales Were on Xbox, With Remaining 91% Shared Between PS5 and Steam
summary_en: Capcom's latest survival horror hit, Resident Evil Requiem, has stormed past $500 million in revenue. A new analysis reveals a stark platform sales disparity, with Xbox significantly trailing behind PlayStation and PC.

en.title: Resident Evil Requiem Sales: Xbox Captures Just 8.6% of $500M Revenue
en.summary: Capcom's latest survival horror hit, Resident Evil Requiem, has stormed past $500 million in revenue. A new analysis reveals a stark platform sales disparity, with Xbox significantly trailing behind PlayStation and PC.
en.body:
The survival horror juggernaut **Resident Evil Requiem** has achieved a monumental financial milestone, surpassing $500 million in global revenue. This impressive figure, bolstered by 8.5 million copies sold across major platforms, cements its status as the fastest-selling title in the storied **Resident Evil** franchise to date. However, a closer examination of the sales data reveals a striking imbalance in platform performance, with the Xbox Series X/S capturing a mere 8.6% of the total units sold.

According to analysis from Alinea Analytics, the lion's share of **Resident Evil Requiem**'s success lies with Sony's **PlayStation 5** and PC via **Steam**. The PS5 accounted for a commanding 48.1% of sales, translating to approximately 4.01 million copies. Meanwhile, PC players via Steam weren't far behind, securing 43.4% of the market, equating to around 3.69 million copies. This leaves Xbox Series X/S with roughly 731,000 units sold, a figure that underscores a significant platform gap in this generation.

## The Xbox Conundrum in Third-Party Dominance

This sales split isn't entirely unexpected, given the broader market trends and console install bases. The PlayStation 5 has consistently held a strong lead in console sales this generation, boasting a substantial installed base that naturally translates to higher unit sales for major multiplatform titles. While the PS5's sales momentum has slowed as it matures, its considerable reach remains a powerful factor. Xbox Series X/S, conversely, has faced considerable headwinds, with Microsoft ceasing to report official sales figures for years. Current estimates place its total units sold significantly below that of its predecessor, the Xbox One, suggesting a more challenging environment for third-party software to reach its full potential on the platform.

## What This Means for Gamers

For fans invested in the **Resident Evil** universe, these numbers offer a clear picture of where the majority of the player base resides. This can influence future development priorities, such as post-launch support, DLC strategies, and even the focus of subsequent titles. While **Resident Evil Requiem** is undeniably a massive success across the board, the performance disparity might lead developers and publishers to further tailor their marketing and platform strategies. It also fuels ongoing discussions within the gaming community about console market share and the unique appeal of each platform for different types of players and game genres.

## Looking Ahead

With **Resident Evil Requiem** continuing its sales trajectory and Capcom's robust pipeline of upcoming titles, including the highly anticipated **Resident Evil 9**, the focus will remain on how these sales patterns evolve. Further analysis of future releases, particularly those with significant cross-platform appeal, will be crucial in understanding the long-term dynamics of the current console generation.

content_raw: Resident Evil Requiem sold just 8.6% of its copies on Xbox, new sales analysis indicates. Data published today by Alinea Analytics revealed the eye-opening split in platform sales for this year's brilliant Resident Evil game, offering yet another glimpse into Xbox's struggles against its rival, Sony's dominant PlayStation 5. Requiem is still selling faster than any other game in Capcom's survival horror series so far and has now passed $500 million in total revenue, with 8.5 million copies shifted across PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. But only 8.6% of that 8.5 million (around 731,000 copies) were sold for Xbox consoles. Compare that to the whopping 48.1% of copies sold on PS5 (around 4.01 million) and the relatively similar 43.4% of copies sold via Steam (around 3.69 million) and it's clear how far behind Xbox is here. On the one hand, this isn't a huge surprise. PS5 has sold well this console generation, with 95.3 million units shipped as of June. Six years into its lifecycle and with hardware prices on the rise, sales momentum has notably slowed. But the machine is guaranteed to get a shot in the arm this fall when GTA 6 arrives, and PS5 is exclusively plastered all over the game's marketing. Xbox Series X/S, on the other hand, has really struggled. Microsoft stopped reporting sales figures years ago, though its current pair of consoles are believed to have sold a little over 35 million units to date — a figure that's worryingly below the unpopular Xbox One, which shifted 58 million units during the last console generation. Today's data on Resident Evil Requiem sales comes just a day after report pointed to a similarly significant sales split for GTA 6 preorders. The Verge 's Tom Warren stated that pre-sales for Rockstar's upcoming blockbuster were "heavily skewed" towards PS5, something that had set off "alarm bells" within Microsoft's Redmond campus. In a statement shared with IGN , Xbox chief strategy office Matthew Ball responded to this claim by stating that, actually, Microsoft was "very happy with GTA 6 preorders," which were "breaking records for Xbox" and "matching our share of the console market." Exactly which records were being broken, though, Ball did not elaborate. Of course, no-one should expect a 50:50 sales split for Resident Evil Requiem or GTA 6 preorders across Sony and Microsoft's consoles.
